items.title: Bob Magnusson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: Shostakovich and all the traditional — Mozart and Brahms.

ctx.x: Cool. Yeah, mentioning being a principal anything in a symphony, that’s such a totally different kind of pressure, like every note has to be — the idea of mistake is so small.

Yeah, we can make a mistake in jazz and move it into something. But they don’t have that luxury there. It’s a different kind of pressure. And I’ve done some orchestra playing on the French horn and on the double bass, and grew up around it, and my dad was marvelous at it, I mean he really did a wonderful job and exposed me to all kinds of great music, Shostakovich and all the traditional — Mozart and Brahms. And then I heard all the woodwind quintet literature, they would rehearse in our house. I remember going…
Of the recordings you’ve done, are there any that stick out in your mind as being your best work?
